newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore jet and diesel rise on Cilacap tank fire.
newsitem.headline: Singapore jet and diesel rise on Cilacap tank fire.

text.p: Singapore diesel and jet fuel prices rose on fears that a fire at one crude tank at Indonesia's Cilacap refinery might disrupt production, traders said on Tuesday.

The fire occured at 1356 hours local time on Monday and was put out within 20 minutes. But speculations were rife in Singapore that the 300,000-bpd refinery might be forced to cut runs, sources said. Traders recalled a fire last year which destroyed seven product tanks and led to a 30-pct drop in crude runs for months. December gas oil swaps rose late Tuesday to trade at $30.23 from a morning low of $29.80, brokers said.
Physical gas oil also picked up with sales done out of Thailand for a mid-December cargo between 20 and 25 cents per barrel premium to Singapore quotes fob.
China has raised its purchases with a December cargo sold earlier $235 per tonne c+f southern China.
Jet fuel prices were boosted further on news of renewed buying from Japan with a mid-December 30,000-tonne cargo sold at $1.75 premium to spot Singapore quotes c+f, traders said.
As a result, December jet fuel/gas oil spreads traded to a high of $1.05, from Monday's 60/80 cents. December jet fuel traded as $31.00 and $31.30.

A 50,000 barrel-cargo of 95-octane unleaded gasoline lifting December 15-19 was traded at $25.40 a barrel, down from Monday's deal at $25.75. Some traders said the level as low even though the naphtha/mogas spread, assessed at $2.30-$2.40, was under pressure as naphtha remained firm.
Naphtha supplies from Singapore refiners for December were still available for December with sellers heard offering at $1.00 a barrel over Singapore quotes, fob.
Fuel oil was steady as players felt that the market had bottomed. Some swaps buying was seen with Dec traded at $117.50, unchanged from Monday. --Singapore Newsroom (+65-870-3093)
